fig01_loop: The feedback loop: the controller acts on the gap between target and measurement.
fig02_openloop: Final position = u/k, so holding 1 m needs u = k*1 = 20 N forever (the spring pulls back).
fig03_measures: Rise time, overshoot, settling time and steady-state error marked on one response.
fig05_sse_check: Simulation dots sit on the formula line: the calculation matches the graphs.
fig06_pi: Adding I drives the error to ~0 but larger Ki adds overshoot/oscillation.
fig07_pd: Kd=0 overshoots ~32 %; Kd=20 gives 0 % overshoot (offset 0.0625 m remains).
fig08_compare: PID is fast, has ~0 overshoot and zero final error; each other combo lacks something.
fig09_windup: Without anti-windup the I term charges up while saturated and causes overshoot; back-calculation removes it.
fig10_noise: Raw D makes the force jitter wildly; a low-pass filter on D cuts the jitter while keeping the response.
fig11_kick: Differentiating the error gives a one-step spike (Kd/dt); differentiating the measurement removes it.
fig12_slow: Slower updates add delay; beyond ~dt = 50 ms these gains oscillate and diverge.
fig13_manual: Typical hand-tuning order: P, then D to tame overshoot, then more P, then a little I.
fig14_zn: Left: P-only sustained swing gives Ku and Pu. Right: table gains are aggressive; reduced gains with D filtering overshoot less.
fig15_final: Final controller: response (top) and how P, I, D add up to the force (bottom; settles at 20 N).
